span.label: THE SAME PARADOX Gotts2012 REVIEWS, AND THIS IS THE EXPERIMENT IT ASKED FOR. Gotts said the four candidate models were `in need of testing`; this paper says why they had not been tested - `noninvasive techniques for human studies have had INSUFFICIENT SPATIAL-TEMPORAL PRECISION for testing their predictions` - and then supplies the precision with electrocorticography. A review naming a gap and a study filling it, two records in one corpus
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THREE EFFECTS, NOT TWO. Beside suppression the study finds repetition ENHANCEMENT at some sites and a TEMPORAL SHIFT to earlier responses at others - `repetition suppression (RS) at some sites, and repetition enhancement (RE) in others, the latter often followed by repetition suppression (~600 ms)`. The paradox as usually stated has two terms; measured at this resolution the cortex does three different things, sometimes in sequence at one site
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE NOVEL EFFECT DOES NOT SURVIVE THE GROUP ANALYSIS, IN THE PAPER'S OWN WORDS: `Quotation withheld` So RE is a per-site observation, reported honestly as one, with the closing verdict that further investigation `is warranted` rather than that the effect is established. The result the abstract calls `interesting` is the one the results section declines to claim at group level
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: WHAT THE ELECTRODES COULD SEE IS A LIMIT ON WHAT WAS FOUND, and the paper says so: `the numbers of sites revealing repetition suppression, repetition enhancement, or temporal shift were LIMITED BY THE ELECTRODE LOCATIONS UNIQUE TO EACH PATIENT`. Coverage is clinical, not experimental - electrodes go where the epilepsy surgery needs them - so absence of an effect at a site is not evidence of its absence in that region. A sampling constraint that no amount of statistics repairs
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: behavioral priming —contrasted-with→ repetition suppression
span.note: differs in: THE DIRECTION EACH MOVES ON THE SAME REPETITION - responses get FASTER while neural activity gets WEAKER. The paper calls it a paradox in the sentence that states it, and the whole study exists to resolve it · strength of the relation: 0.95 — The same contrast tagged on Gotts2012 forty minutes earlier, from a review; here it is from the experiment that tests it. Two records, one paradox, and the corpus can now hold the review's inventory beside the measurement.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: predictive coding —causes→ repetition suppression
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.85 — THE EVIDENCE IS A TIMING CLAIM: the top-down propagation PRECEDED the suppression, which is what makes it a candidate cause rather than a correlate. Weighted 0.85 - `provide support for` is the paper's own strength, and precedence is necessary but not sufficient for the model.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: repetition enhancement —distinct-from→ repetition suppression
span.note: differs in: THE SIGN OF THE NEURAL CHANGE AT A SITE - enhancement is more activity with repetition, suppression is less, and the two occur at different electrodes in the same patients, sometimes in sequence at one site with enhancement followed by suppression around 600 ms · strength of the relation: 0.8 — Weight 0.8 and NOT higher, because of the group analysis: RE `did not reach statistical significance for VOTC, LPFC, or OAS`. The distinction is real at individual sites and unestablished at group level, and the sense row carries that. Recording this at 0.95 would assert what the results section declines to claim.

span.label: Behavioral priming was accompanied by suppressed high gamma activity in ventral occipito-temporal cortex, left prefrontal cortex and other activated sites, plus a shift of activity to earlier time points in sensorimotor regions that mediate speaking.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Repetition also increased activation at 30 sites in lateral frontal, parietal and temporal cortex, but never in ventral occipito-temporal cortex, so repetition enhancement and suppression occupy different territory.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Repeated stimuli produced a statistically significant increase in high gamma propagation from left prefrontal cortex into ventral occipito-temporal cortex beginning about 100 ms after stimulus onset.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The repetition-related rise in top-down propagation became significant before repetition suppression appeared in VOTC, putting the top-down change first in the causal order.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Within individual patients the dominant direction of flow reversed with repetition: novel stimuli drove propagation bottom-up from VOTC to LPFC, whereas repeated stimuli drove it top-down from LPFC to VOTC.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The facilitation model's central prediction failed in ventral occipito-temporal cortex: repeated trials showed no consistent shift of the activation envelope to earlier latencies, only a reduced peak and an earlier return to baseline.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Repetition suppression emerged in ventral occipito-temporal cortex at about 140 ms but only reached significance in left prefrontal cortex at about 280 ms.
